anchor.quote: A treaty is an international agreement that is binding under international law. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade explains the different types of treaties and how they are made in the Treaty making process.

not_rules.note: Defines what a treaty is and refers to external guidance.

anchor.quote: Sometimes a Commonwealth Act of parliament is required to give effect to a treaty – for example, the Antarctic Treaty Act 1960.

not_rules.note: Background information about treaty implementation in Australian law.

anchor.quote: Treaties also include conventions, international agreements, covenants, an exchange of letters, international instruments, charters or protocols.

not_rules.note: Definitional description of what instruments constitute treaties.

anchor.quote: Treaties appear in various official series published by countries and international organisations.

not_rules.note: Descriptive background on treaty series publications.

anchor.quote: Australian treaties are published in the Australian Treaty Series (ATS). Other series include the United Nations Treaty Series (UNTS), the United States Treaties and Other International Agreements (UST) and the United Kingdom Treaty Series (UKTS).

not_rules.note: Descriptive information listing treaty publication series.

anchor.quote: To search for the titles, short titles and series information for treaties that Australia has signed or taken other action on, use the Australian Treaties Database. You can also use AustLII’s Australian Treaties Library.

not_rules.note: Advice to the writer on research sources and tools (G-5).

anchor.quote: For other series, use the WorldLII Treaties and International Agreements database catalogue. Alternatively, go directly to the relevant databases. These include the United Nations Treaty Collection, UK Treaties Online and, for the US, Treaties and Other International Acts Series.

not_rules.note: Advice to the writer on databases to search (G-5).

anchor.quote: In general publications, citing the title of the treaty is usually enough.

covers.quote: Style for treaty titles is roman type, title case

examples.note: Treaty title in roman type and title case.

parts.quote: The South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty (SPNFP) is also known as the Treaty of Rarotonga.

rules.quote: Write titles of treaties in roman type with title case (maximal capitalisation).
rules.violation_condition: a treaty title written in italics or without title case (maximal capitalisation)

examples.note: Short title in parentheses following full title.

parts.quote: The South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty (SPNFP) is also known as the Treaty of Rarotonga.

examples.note: Full title followed by short title in parentheses, with short title used in subsequent sentence.

parts.quote: Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal (Basel Convention). Australian signed the Basel Convention in 1992.

rules.quote: Follow the full title with the short title in parentheses and use the short title after that.
rules.violation_condition: introducing a treaty short title without enclosing it in parentheses after the full title, or continuing to use the full title rather than the short title after introduction
rules.why: Distinct requirement governing the presentation and subsequent use of treaty short titles.

examples.note: Year of making added in parentheses after the short title.

parts.quote: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) (1966)

rules.quote: The year the treaty is made does not form part of the title. If you include it, write it into the sentence or add it in parentheses after the short title.
rules.violation_condition: the year of making included as part of the treaty title rather than written into the running text or placed in parentheses after the short title
when: When including the year the treaty was made, it may be written into the sentence or placed in parentheses after the short title.
rules.why: Prohibits treating the year of making as part of the title, with specified exceptions for how to include it (G-2, G-3).

covers.quote: page number in the series volume.
Don’t use any punctuation between the elements.
If a short title has been introduced and used in the text, you can use the short title in the note.

examples.note: Detailed citation elements ordered correctly with no punctuation between elements.

parts.quote: Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal (Basel, 22 March 1989) [1992] UNTS 1673 p 57.

examples.note: Detailed citation without trailing page number.

parts.quote: Singapore–Australia Free Trade Agreement (Singapore, 17 February 2003) [2003] ATS 16.

examples.note: Detailed citation citing multiple treaty series.

parts.quote: South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty (Rarotonga, 6 August 1985) [1986] ATS 32, UNTS 1445 p 177; ILM 24 p 1440; NZTS 1986/7.

rules.violation_condition: a detailed treaty citation that does not order the elements as title, (place of making, date of making), [year treaty entered into force], treaty series and volume number, page number in the series volume, or that includes punctuation between the elements
when: In notes, a short title may be used instead of the full title if the short title has already been introduced in text.
rules.why: 8b6e2e02581b leads into the citation template items and the punctuation instruction in eff051543a39; 447ef713c6a6 is a permission for notes (G-2, G-3).

examples.note: Reference list citation using the full long title.

parts.quote: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (New York, 16 December 1966) [1980] ATS 23.

rules.quote: Always use the long title in a reference list.
rules.violation_condition: a treaty entry in a reference list using a short title instead of the full long title
when: Applies to treaty citations in reference lists.
rules.why: Mandatory requirement specifying full long titles in reference lists, contrasting with note permissions.
